subject: Data disposition & log-retention evidence request — MedAtlas
messages:
From: Gina Park <gina.park@medatlas.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: evidence for shorter log disposition window (MedAtlas)

Hi Vanessa / Marcus,

Quick background: MedAtlas is finalizing our partner integration security review and we have a policy requirement that certain application logs and request traces for PHI-touching endpoints be retained for a maximum of 90 days unless a variance is approved by our security council. Your current public docs list 12–24 months for audit logs; our InfoSec team needs: 1) technical evidence that Redwood can enforce a per-tenant log TTL of 90 days (including proof of deletion), and 2) an operational attestation or process doc describing how deletions are audited and how we can request evidence for a specific tenant.

Can you provide the artifacts below? If you can send a consolidated package that we can attach to our SIG review that would be ideal.

- A one-page attestation that Redwood can set and enforce a 90-day log TTL per tenant
- Operational evidence: example lifecycle rules / job names (no full-access keys) and expected deletion timestamps for a sample tenant
- Proof-of-deletion sample (anonymized audit entry or job run ID) that shows a deletion for a tenant at 90 days

We are trying to close this week. If you can share a timeline for delivery and whether Legal needs to sign anything (attestation), please let me know.

Thanks,
Gina
Gina Park
Sr. InfoSec Program Manager, MedAtlas

Hi Gina — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Marcus (Security) and Mina (CS) so we can get the right artifacts over. High level: we do support per-tenant log TTLs and have an auditable deletion pipeline, but we need to validate what evidence we can provide without exposing other customers.

Next steps I propose:
- Marcus: prepare a technical packet (lifecycle rules, job names, anonymized audit lines) + one-page attestation language for Legal to review
- Mina: coordinate with the customer on how they want proof delivered (PDF bundle vs DocuSign attestation) and confirm whether MedAtlas' InfoSec is okay with anonymized job IDs rather than full object lists
- Vanessa: I'll coordinate Legal if an official signed attestation is needed; also will open an internal ticket to capture the exact tenant example we can use for proof-of-deletion

Can you confirm whether the 90-day requirement is absolute (hard stop) or if your council would accept a signed variance from Redwood? Also — are you requesting retention changes for all logs or only PHI-touching traces? That will determine scope.

I can push an initial packet by EOD Tuesday PST (2026-11-03). Does that work?

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Request: evidence for shorter log disposition window (MedAtlas)

Vanessa / Gina —

Thanks for the context. Below is the technical packet we can provide; attaching a redwood-sig-evidence-2026-11.pdf with screenshots and anonymized entries, plus a CSV TTL matrix. Summary:

1) Per-tenant TTL enforcement
- We support tenant-scoped lifecycle rules at the object-prefix layer and a scheduled garbage-collector job (gc-tenant-ttl) that reconciles object metadata and issues deletions.
- Rule examples: S3 lifecycle rule name = rw-logs-tenant-ttl, retentionDays = 90 (configurable). We can set this per-tenant on request or as part of onboarding config.

2) Proof-of-deletion and auditability
- Deletions are recorded in our audit stream (immutable append-only log) with job run IDs and SHA256 of object manifest. We can provide anonymized job run IDs and associated timestamps.
- Sample anonymized audit entry (redacted): 2026-08-15T03:22:11Z | gc-tenant-ttl | tenant=redacted-tenant-42 | deletedObjects=137 | jobRunID=jr_6f3a2b

3) Operational attestation draft
- Attached is a one-page attestation draft we typically use. Legal will need to review language and sign.

Limitations / notes:
- We cannot provide raw object names or full manifests that would reveal other customers' identifiers.
- If MedAtlas requires signed attestation for a shorter-than-default retention, we will coordinate Legal; that typically takes 3–5 business days after we confirm final language.

Deliverables attached: redwood-sig-evidence-2026-11.pdf, redwood-log-ttl-matrix.csv, redwood-retention-attestation-draft.docx

Let me know if you need a tenant-specific sample; we can schedule a short call with our SRE to pull a sanitized audit run.

—
Marcus Lin
Security Lead, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

Hi Vanessa / Marcus —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments. The packet looks reasonable to our InfoSec team; they have two follow-ups before we can mark this closed:

1) We need a signed attestation stating Redwood will enforce a 90-day TTL for the MedAtlas tenant and that audit records will be made available upon request in anonymized form. Please confirm whether Redwood Legal can sign the attestation draft attached. We can accept DocuSign.
2) We would like one anonymized proof-of-deletion sample for a tenant similar in size to MedAtlas (100–250k objects deleted) showing the jobRunID and timestamp. The sample can be redacted to remove object names.

If Redwood can provide both items, we will proceed to mark the SIG review as satisfied. Our deadline is COB Friday 2026-11-06. Please advise on timing and who at Redwood will own the DocuSign flow.

Best regards,
MedAtlas Legal Ops
legalops@medatlas.com
